## Introduction

This appendix provides detailed specifications and results for the two survival models developed in the colorectal cancer (CRC) case study. These models aim to highlight:

1.  The non-linear effect (NLE) of Age.\
2.  The time-varying effect (TVE) of Surgery.

All analyses were performed using the `rstpm2` package for flexible survival models. The dataset was cleaned and preprocessed to include only the covariates relevant to our case study.

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Data preparation (complete records of the analysis variables, see R/utils_case_study.R)
suppressMessages({
  library(tidyverse); library(rstpm2); library(broom); library(survival)
  library(survminer); library(purrr)
})
source("../R/utils_case_study.R")

set.seed(1234)

CRC <- read_CRC("../data/CRC.csv")
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Proportional Hazards assumption and functional form diagnostics

Before fitting flexible survival models, we assessed the proportional hazards (PH) assumption and the functional form of covariates.

### Schoenfeld residual tests

```{r, echo = FALSE}
# Cox model for PH testing
cox_model <- coxph(Surv(time, event) ~ Age + Surgery +
                     MSI.MSS.status + Sex + Stage, data = CRC)
ph_test <- cox.zph(cox_model)
print(ph_test)
```

Significant p-values for Age and Surgery indicate violations of the proportional hazards assumption.

### Schoenfeld residual plots

```{r, echo = FALSE, fig.cap="Schoenfeld residuals for Age"}
ggcoxzph(ph_test, var = "Age")
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, fig.cap="Schoenfeld residuals for Surgery"}
ggcoxzph(ph_test, var = "Surgery")
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Martingale residuals for age

```{r, echo = FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.cap="Martingale residuals for Age"}
CRC$martingale <- residuals(cox_model, type = "martingale")

ggplot(CRC, aes(Age, martingale)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE, color = "blue") +
  labs(
    title = "Martingale Residuals vs Age",
    x = "Age",
    y = "Martingale Residuals"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

The plot reveals a convex, non-linear pattern for Age, with relatively stable risk in midlife and increasing hazard at older ages, supporting the use of a flexible modeling approach.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Degrees of Freedom (df) selection

To select the optimal spline complexity, AIC was computed across multiple degrees of freedom.

### For age

```{r, echo=FALSE}
rng_age <- range(CRC$Age)
aic_stpm2 <- function(model) 2 * model@min + 2 * length(coef(model))
fit_lin <- stpm2(Surv(time, event) ~ Age + Surgery + MSI.MSS.status + Sex + Stage,
                 data = CRC)
dfs_age <- 1:6
aic_results_age <- map_dfr(dfs_age, function(df) {
  fit_df <- stpm2(Surv(time, event) ~ nsx(Age, df = df, Boundary.knots = rng_age) +
                    Surgery + MSI.MSS.status + Sex + Stage,
                  data = CRC)
  tibble(model = paste0("natural spline, df = ", df), AIC = aic_stpm2(fit_df))
})
aic_results_age <- bind_rows(tibble(model = "linear", AIC = aic_stpm2(fit_lin)),
                             aic_results_age)
as.data.frame(mutate(aic_results_age, AIC = round(AIC, 1)))
```

The NLE of Age is modeled with a natural cubic spline of Age in the linear predictor. The AIC values were close across specifications (linear age and spline df from 1 to 6), so the data give weak support for departure from linearity. We retained df = 4, which allows a U-shaped or asymmetric pattern without the instability of higher df.

### For surgery

```{r}
dfs_surgery <- 2:4
aic_results_surgery <- map_dfr(dfs_surgery, function(df) {
  model <- stpm2(Surv(time, event) ~ Age + Surgery + MSI.MSS.status + Sex + Stage,
                 data = CRC,
                 tvc = list(Surgery = df))
  tibble(df = df, AIC = AIC(model))
})
aic_results_surgery
```

Although the model with df = 4 yielded the lowest AIC for Surgery, the resulting time-varying hazard curve exhibited implausible fluctuations and lacked clinical interpretability. For this reason, a more parsimonious model with df = 3 was retained, as it provided a smoother and more consistent representation of the time-varying effect, better aligned with clinical plausibility and visual diagnostics.

## Model 1: Non-Linear Effect (NLE) of age

A flexible survival model capturing the non-linear effect of Age with a natural cubic spline of Age with 4 degrees of freedom:

```{r}
fit_Age <- stpm2(
  Surv(time, event) ~ nsx(Age, df = 4, Boundary.knots = rng_age) +
    Surgery + MSI.MSS.status + Sex + Stage,
  data = CRC
)
summary(fit_Age)
```

```{r, warning=FALSE, fig.cap="Non-linear effect of Age: hazard ratio relative to age 60 years (log scale)"}
age_grid <- seq(25, 85, by = 1)
age_grid <- age_grid[age_grid >= rng_age[1] & age_grid <= rng_age[2]]
nd_age <- data.frame(time = 12, Age = age_grid, Surgery = 0,
                     MSI.MSS.status = 0, Sex = 0, Stage = 1)
ref_age <- transform(nd_age, Age = 60)
hr_age <- data.frame(
  Age = age_grid,
  HR = predict(fit_Age, newdata = nd_age, type = "haz") /
    predict(fit_Age, newdata = ref_age, type = "haz")
)
ggplot(hr_age, aes(Age, HR)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "HR (Age vs 60)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Model 2: Time-Varying Effect (TVE) of surgery

A flexible survival model capturing the time-varying effect of Surgery using 3 degrees of freedom:

```{r}
fit_Surgery <- stpm2(
  Surv(time, event) ~ Age + Surgery + 
    MSI.MSS.status + Sex + Stage,
  data = CRC,
  tvc = list(Surgery = 3)
)
summary(fit_Surgery)
```

```{r, eval=FALSE, fig.cap="Time-varying Hazard Ratio for Surgery"}
### Plot of hazard ratio of surgery over time

n <- nrow(CRC) + 1
surgery_pred <- predict(fit_Surgery, type = "link",
                        newdata = data.frame(Age = 60, Surgery = 1, MSI.MSS.status = 0, Sex = 0, Stage = 1),
                        grid = TRUE, seqLength = n, full = TRUE, se.fit = TRUE)

surgery_pred <- surgery_pred %>%
  mutate(
    HR = exp(Estimate),
    HR_lower = exp(lower),
    HR_upper = exp(upper)
  )

ggplot(surgery_pred, aes(x = time, y = HR)) +
  geom_line(color = "blue") +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = HR_lower, ymax = HR_upper), alpha = 0.2) +
  labs(
    title = "Time-varying Hazard Ratio for Surgery",
    x = "Time (years)",
    y = "Hazard Ratio (Surgery)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Conclusion

This appendix presents diagnostic checks and detailed flexible modeling strategies used to examine non-linear and time-varying effects in the CRC survival analysis case study. The findings support the application of spline-based models to uncover complex covariate behavior over time and across distributions.
